task.summary: Default task
style: correct Chances and SetMapSize comments
feat(core): port Terrain, BArray, Challenges, Statistics, Assets, ResultDescriptions, Utils
feat(core): port the Level map shell, Painter, ShadowCaster, and Dungeon shell
feat(core): port Actor, Buff, Char, Door, field of view, and the hero and mob shells
feat(core): port Ballistica and the Dungeon path helpers
feat(core): port Room, Patch, the four basic painters, and RegularLevel room layout
feat(core): port the Level create pipeline, drop, press, chasm, high grass, sign, and level bundling
feat(core): port SewerLevel with generation invariants
feat(core): port Hero with move, stairs, search, rest, chasm, sign, and death
feat(core): port Dungeon init, level switching, the in-memory level store, and Interlevel transitions
feat(view): render the level as placeholder cells with three fog states
feat(view): add the hero view, the follow camera, and the per-frame scheduler pump
feat(view): click and keyboard cell selection feeding Hero.Handle fix(view): camera shake decays over its duration
feat(view): status pane, message and choice windows, and the faded level switch
feat(view): text debug console with depth, reveal, seed, where, and help fix(view): release the fade and the switching flag even when a level switch fails
fix(view): defer the level switch with a statement lambda so Godot does not convert the Task. Depth recovers from a failed transition; stairs command and startup console

docs: sub-project 1 complete; README status and plan notes fix: final review wave: reset the chasm confirmation, turn the hero view, null the freed sprite, clear the seam on exit, cover the dr roll; docs corrected

feat(seam): mob views, attack, alert, and game over ICharView gains Attack/ShowAlert/HideAlert; IGameView gains AddMob and GameOver. ShowSleep/HideSleep are deliberately absent: the Java derives the sleep icon by polling mob.state, so the view polls too. GameScene.Add(Mob[, delay]) keeps the level bookkeeping, scheduling and cell occupancy in Core and sends only the sprite across the seam, so NullGameView stays inert without swallowing a mob.

feat(mobs): damage, death, experience and loot Damage recovers from Terror and wakes a sleeper to Wandering. DefenseSkill returns 0 until the mob has seen someone, which is the sneak-attack rule. Destroy grants experience and moves the run counters, Die drops loot only while the hero is within MaxLvl + 2. DropLoot ports its full dispatch and that gate so both are testable now, but the Gnoll, Crab and Swarm loot fields stay DEFERRED(sp3) because Gold, MysteryMeat and PotionOfHealing are for later

feat(mobs): Rat, Albino, Gnoll and Crab Stat blocks copied verbatim, with tests that assert every number against the Java rather than against the implementation. Albino subclasses Rat as in the original and adds the 1-in-2 Bleeding proc; Crab keeps its speed of 2 and its "parried" defense verb.

feat(mobs): Swarm and its split The split ports in full. HP >= damage + 2 gate, the orthogonal-only candidate cells, the (HP - damage) / 2 clone, the generation counter, the clone entering HUNTING, and Door.Enter when it lands in a doorway, and is tested by calling DefenseProc directly, so its 1-in-200 spawn rate does not gate verification. TODO: pusihing, the clone appears at its cell instead of sliding. Burning and Poison propagation and the PotionOfHealing drop are likewise deferred to the sub-projects that bring those classes.

feat(mobs): the whole Bestiary table behind a type registry All 25 depths port verbatim as chance/name pairs. A Dictionary<Type, Func> holds factories for the ported classes; entries naming an unported class are dropped before the roll, and a depth with nothing registered returns null, which the existing guards in RegularLevel.CreateMobs and Level.RespawnerActor already handle. Later sub-projects add a mob by registering a factory. The table is written once and never edited again. The depth-4 distribution loses Skeleton and Thief (0.02 of 6.04 weight) until later projects, and depths 5 and up spawn nothing until theirs. Both are asserted by tests so the deviation stays visible.

feat(hero): attack action, regeneration, and the crippling fall ActAttack ports verbatim: an adjacent living enemy that has not charmed the hero gets a swing, which returns false and holds the scheduler until the view calls OnAttackComplete; anything else steps closer or hands control back. Live attaches Regeneration, without which the hero never heals and Rest(tillHealthy) never terminates. The respawner now wakes its mob into WANDERING and registers it with the scene, and a chasm landing cripples the hero.

feat(view): attack tween and the emo glyph Attack turns toward the target, lunges a third of a cell and returns, then calls OnAttackComplete. It reuses Move's kill-and-reset discipline, so an interrupted swing cannot strand the scheduler. One Label3D holds one glyph at a time, "!" for alert and "z" for sleep, mirroring CharSprite's single emo field. Alert is pushed through the seam, sleep is derived per frame from mob.state, as MobSprite does in the Java.

feat(view): mob cubes, per-frame reconcile, and a game-over window One CharView per mob in a species colour, rebuilt on every level switch. A single per-frame pass frees views whose mob has left the level, sets visibility from the field of view, and derives the sleep glyph from mob.State, which is what the Java's MobSprite.update does, and which covers death, chasm falls, Swarm splits and respawns through one path. The free path also calls Actor.Next() before queuing the view free: killing a live tween via InterruptMotion() never raises Finished, so if the freed mob were ever Actor._current (frozen mid its own attack tween), nothing would clear that pointer and the scheduler would stop dispatching turns to every actor. Next() is a no-op for any mob that isn't current, so this closes the gap at no cost. GameOver reads Dungeon.ResultDescription into the existing window with Restart and Quit. Sub-project 10 replaces the body; the call site is done.

feat(view): XP readout and the spawn/kill debug commands The status pane gains hero level and experience beside HP and depth. spawn [n] places mobs on free cells around the hero and kill destroys every mob in sight through Die, so experience, loot and the death log all run. These are what make depths 1 to 4 testable without grinding. kill recomputes Level.FieldOfView for the hero via Dungeon.Observe() before reading it: the buffer is one shared static array that every actor's Act() overwrites with its own viewshed, so without recomputing it kill could act on whatever mob last moved instead of what the hero can see.

feat: sub-project 2 complete, fight through the Sewers and die Two integration tests close the loop: killing a rat earns its experience and moves the run counters, and dying to one records the cause in Dungeon.ResultDescription and reaches GameScene.GameOver. ReallyDie now calls GameOver. README and the roadmap record sub-project 2 as complete.

fix: game-over cause, mob visibility buffer, and death-window input lock Every death path (melee, chasm fall, bleeding) called GameScene.GameOver() from Hero.ReallyDie() before Dungeon.Fail() had a chance to run and set Dungeon.ResultDescription, so the "You died" window's first line was always blank. The Java gets away with the identical call order because its gameOver() only shows a banner and the rankings scene reads the cause much later; porting the call site verbatim without porting that laziness broke it here. GameOver() now defers building the window body by one frame (Callable.From(ShowDeathWindow).CallDeferred(), a method reference rather than an expression lambda per this project's earlier lambda-to-Task lesson), so the cause is always populated by the time the window reads it. Verified live in a headless run against both the fixed and reverted code: the reverted version prints ResultDescription='' at GameOver() time, the fix prints the real cause. That same GameOver() call bypassed the counted ShowWindow(request) path, so the death window never disabled CellSelector's input. Hero.Die clears CurAction but not Ready, so WASD behind the window still reached Handle() and could make a corpse walk and fight. GameOver() now routes through ShowWindow(request), and CellSelector's process and select paths also require Dungeon.Hero.IsAlive() as belt-and-braces. Restart's interaction with the open-window counter was traced end to end: the dialog's Confirmed handler runs Restart() synchronously before the dialog hides, so the counter always lands back on zero. GameScene's per-frame mob-visibility reconcile and AddMob both read Level.FieldOfView, a scratch buffer every Char.Act() overwrites with its own viewshed, mobs included. Reading it after a mob's turn shows the mob's view, not the hero's, so visible mobs could vanish and hidden ones pop into view for the length of an attack tween, and wrongly-hidden mobs would teleport instead of sliding. Both sites now read Dungeon.Visible. Finally, the death integration test asserted only end-of-test state, so it could not detect the ordering defect above: Dungeon.Fail() does run eventually, just after GameOver() rather than before. RecordingGameView now captures ResultDescription at the moment GameOver() is called, and the test asserts that capture is null, the honest, by-design contract on the Core side, which is exactly what the Godot-side deferral works around.

feat(seam): heap views, cell listeners, missiles, and zap Heap.Sprite becomes an IHeapView assigned by the view, as Mob.Sprite is, so every level.drop(...).sprite.drop() call site ports verbatim. IGameView gains PickUp, SelectCell, Missile and RefreshQuickSlots; ICharView gains Zap. NullGameView completes a missile at once, so Core throws resolve synchronously without a view. The Godot view stubs the new members, TODO.

feat(items): item values, the sprite sheet ids, and the quick slot model Item gains its level, durability, curse and identification state, the four ToString formats, ConsiderState and bundling. Restoring replays the level through Upgrade, which sets cursedKnown exactly as the Java does. QuickSlot's logic half moves to Core: the slotted values, the per-item bundle flags, Compress, and the last throw target. ItemSpriteSheet's ids port as constants so item initialisers copy verbatim.

feat(items): bags, the key ring, and collecting and detaching items Item gains Collect, Detach, DetachAll and DoPickUp. Bags take matching items first, stacks merge by class, and a full container logs and refuses. The backpack re-sorts by Generator category after every collect, with a stable sort: Java's Collections.sort is stable and List.Sort is not. Key, Bag and Keyring port whole; Belongings gains its 19-slot backpack.

feat(items): belongings, the three keys, and the key ring at start Belongings ports whole: the equipped-then-backpack enumeration, typed and by-class lookups, key lookup by exact class and depth, the iron key count, identify, observe, resurrect and bundling. Weapon, armour and ring slots stay typed Item until their classes are ported. Every new hero collects a key ring, the one initCommon line that needs nothing from a later slice. QuickSlot gains its class form, resolved by name through Bundle's type lookup. Bundle.ResolveType now guards a null/empty name instead of letting Assembly.GetType throw: Bundle.GetString returns "" for a missing key (matching Java's JSONObject.optString), and QuickSlot.Restore's class form has no surrounding try/catch, so an absent quickslot2 key would otherwise throw instead of leaving the slot empty.

feat(items): the generator tables behind a registry, and gold Generator ports all ten category tables verbatim and filters every roll through a type registry, as the Bestiary does. Only Gold is registered, so every random item is gold until 3b and 3c register theirs, a test records the deviation. Weights halve per roll and reset on every level transition, as InterlevelScene resets them. Gold ports whole, and Gnolls drop it. Updated two older tests whose expectations assumed Generator was still a skeleton (LevelPipelineTests.RegularLevel_CreateItems_..., renamed to ...DropsGoldHeaps..., SewerLevelTests.Border_IsImpassable_AndHasNoHeapsYet, renamed to Border_IsImpassable) now that level generation drops real gold heaps.

feat(items): drop, throw, and opening a bag Item gains Actions, Execute, DoDrop, DoThrow, OnThrow and Cast. A throw asks the view for a cell through the thrower listener, traces a Ballistica bolt that stops on the first char, and hands the view a missile whose completion detaches one item, lands it, and spends the turn, so the hero stays Actor._current while it flies, exactly as in the Java. A test holds the missile and proves the scheduler waits. A bag's default action shows it through the new IGameView.ShowBag.

feat(items): dewdrops, the dew vial, and the death save Dewdrops heal on pick-up or fill the vial; the vial drinks through the operate gate, spawns in the Sewers while its flag is set, and saves a dying hero when full. Trampled high grass drops dew on its 1-in-6 roll, the seed roll still runs but drops nothing until seeds are registered. A test pins a float edge: a full vial heals 21 at HT 20, visible only when auto-drink runs with HP below zero.

feat(items): heaps open, merge, pick up, and destroy Heap ports whole apart from burning, freezing and alchemy. Stacks merge and move to the front, a dewdrop goes to the back, and an emptied heap removes itself and kills its view. Opening takes the Java's own no-mimic and no-wraith branches: a mimic opens as a plain chest and a cursed skeleton costs half the hero's HP for now.

feat(hero): pick up, open chests, unlock doors, and scatter on death The hero's PickUp, OpenChest and Unlock actions port verbatim, with the key consumed when the operate animation ends. Death scatters the backpack over free neighbouring cells. AttackIndicator's logic half moves to Core, since its choice among adjacent enemies consumes the game's RNG. Items that fell down a chasm land through GameScene.LandDroppedItems, so the loop from GameScene.create is testable in Core. Wiring AttackIndicator.UpdateState() into Hero.Act() makes it spend one Random draw per turn once a mob is visible and adjacent (matching the Java's Random.element(candidates), which draws even for a one-candidate list). That shifts the RNG stream one position earlier than before, which flipped a pre-existing seeded assertion in HeroCombatTests (OnAttackComplete_AfterASwing_DamagesTheRatAndFreesTheScheduler): its 1-damage swing against a Rat's Dr()==1 is a coin flip on the very next draw. Reseeded immediately before that swing, with a comment, following the same mid-test reseed convention already used elsewhere (MobAiTests, PatchTests, DewTests) to pin a specific roll.

feat(view): heap cubes, thrown items, and chasm landings HeapView implements IHeapView: a box in the top item's colour that hops when dropped, arcs in from another cell, pulses while its item glows and dims under the fog. Discarded heaps shrink away. MissileView flies a thrown item at the Java's 15 cells per second and completes the throw exactly once. Items that fell down a chasm land when the level below is built.

feat(view): cell listeners, the prompt toast, and examine The cell selector hands the next click to a pending listener and restoresHero.Handle afterwards, as CellSelector.select and GameScene.ready do. Escape or the toast cancels with null. Throws now ask for their target. Examine follows Toolbar.informer's branch order and describes cells, mobs and heaps through the existing window.

feat(view): the backpack and item windows WndBag lays out the Java's landscape grid: equipment slots, the bag's items, free slots, the gold slot, and a tab per bag held. Right-clicking an item with a default action puts it in the first quick slot. WndItem lists the item's actions and runs the one chosen. Both count toward the open-window gate that disables input.

feat(view): the toolbar, two quick slots, and item keys The toolbar mirrors the Java's strip: wait, search and examine on the left, backpack and both quick slots on the right, enabled only while the hero is ready. Quick slots resolve instances or classes from Core's model, use their item on click, and choose one on right-click or an empty click. Picked-up items fly into the backpack button. I opens the backpack, 1 and 2 use the slots, and G picks up what lies underfoot.

feat(view): gold, loot and attack indicators, and the iron-key count The gold total appears for two seconds whenever it changes. The loot indicator shows what lies underfoot while the hero is ready and picks it up on click, the attack indicator shows Core's chosen adjacent enemy in its species colour and attacks it. The status pane counts this depth's iron keys.

feat(view): give, heap, lock and fill console commands Keys, locked chests and locked doors come only from special rooms and bosses in the original, so these commands are what make every item branch of this sub-project playable on depth 1. depth and stairs now refuse while the hero is busy, so a thrown item cannot land on the wrong level.

test: item integration tests, and a minor fix Generated Sewer levels carry only gold and the dew vial in non-empty heaps, every item class constructs by type, a hero walks to distant gold and picks it up through the scheduler, and heaps survive leaving a level and coming back.

fix(view): bags cancel a pending cell selection, and scene builds reset gold and iron-key counts A: WndBag.OpenBag now cancels any pending cell selector before it opens (scenes/GameScene.java show -> cancelCellSelector), so leaving a THROW listener armed and then opening the backpack no longer throws on the next floor click. SelectItem no longer duplicates the check. B: WndBag hands its listener null on any close that is not a choice (windows/WndBag.java onBackPressed), via a VisibilityChanged handler guarded by a new _chosen flag set right before every choice's own Hide() call (a slot pick, a tab switch). C: GoldIndicator gets a ResetState() that GameScene.Build calls, so a level switch or Restart no longer shows the previous run's stale gold total. Confirmed against the Java: GoldIndicator is built fresh inside Toolbar.createChildren (ui/Toolbar.java), and Toolbar itself is rebuilt by GameScene.create() on every scene, including Restart. D: GameScene.Build recounts iron keys (Belongings.CountIronKeys) before RefreshQuickSlots, matching ui/StatusPane.java's createChildren, so the "Iron keys" readout no longer sticks to the previous depth's count after a level switch, console jump, or restart.

test: turn costs of item actions, and a lettered marker in MobAiTests F: MobAiTests' bare "DEFERRED(sp3): armour/Barkskin" comment violates the lettered-marker rule and was invisible to the marker audit (which scans only src/ and scripts/). Split it into "TODO: armour, TODO: Barkskin", matching where each actually lands. G: adds six turn-cost assertions the design spec's "## Tests" section calls for but nothing checked: a drop spends TIME_TO_DROP, a completed throw spends TIME_TO_THROW, a cancelled throw spends nothing, an adjacent chest spends TIME_TO_UNLOCK before OnOperateComplete, drinking the dew vial spends 1, and a pick-up spends 1. Each is a small sibling Fact next to the behaviour test it pins, using a shared SpyHero (moved from HeroTests into DungeonFixture so ItemActionTests, HeroItemTests and DewTests can all read Cooldown()). The drop and throw assertions were proven to bite: temporarily changing TIME_TO_DROP to 0.75f failed ExecuteDrop_SpendsTimeToDrop (expected 0.5, got 0.75), and TIME_TO_THROW to 1.5f failed Throw_Completed_SpendsTimeToThrow (expected 1, got 1.5), both constants were then reverted.

feat(core): buff icons and the armour-tier seam member BuffIndicator carries every constant from the Java. Buff.Icon() returns NONE unless a buff overrides it, and Amok, Terror, Cripple and Bleeding now do. ICharView gains UpdateArmor(int tier) for Armor's equip hooks: the null view ignores it, the test fake records each tier, and the Godot CharView stubs it until later.

feat(buffs): Poison, Paralysis, Slow and Roots The four afflictions port whole. Poison deals (int)(left / 3) + 1 a turn and records its death cause. Paralysis and Roots set and clear their Char flags, and Roots will not take hold of a flyer. Slow halves Char.Spend's time scale, so every action takes twice as long. Ring of Elements and the Frost check stay TODO.

feat(actors): affliction status texts, hero warnings and the snap-out Poison and Paralysis ship complete, as the 3b spec decides: - Char.Add shows "poisoned" with a poison splash, and "slowed", "paralysed" and "rooted". - Hero.Add warns on Paralysis, Poison and Roots, and the first two interrupt. - Char.Damage rolls Random.Int(dmg) against Random.Int(HP) to snap a paralysed character out, logging it when visible. - A poisoned Swarm splits into a clone poisoned for 2. The shared markers are split. Burning, Frost, Vertigo, Ooze and the rest stay TODO. MindVision, Levitation and Invisibility stay sp3c. The paralysed sprite state draws nothing, because the cubes have no animation to pause.

I opens the backpack, 1 and 2 use the slots, and G picks up what lies underfoot.

feat(view): gold, loot and attack indicators, and the iron-key count The gold total appears for two seconds whenever it changes. The loot indicator shows what lies underfoot while the hero is ready and picks it up on click, the attack indicator shows Core's chosen adjacent enemy in its species colour and attacks it. The status pane counts this depth's iron keys.

feat(view): give, heap, lock and fill console commands Keys, locked chests and locked doors come only from special rooms and bosses in the original, so these commands are what make every item branch of this sub-project playable on depth 1. depth and stairs now refuse while the hero is busy, so a thrown item cannot land on the wrong level.

test: item integration tests, and a minor fix Generated Sewer levels carry only gold and the dew vial in non-empty heaps, every item class constructs by type, a hero walks to distant gold and picks it up through the scheduler, and heaps survive leaving a level and coming back.

fix(view): bags cancel a pending cell selection, and scene builds reset gold and iron-key counts A: WndBag.OpenBag now cancels any pending cell selector before it opens (scenes/GameScene.java show -> cancelCellSelector), so leaving a THROW listener armed and then opening the backpack no longer throws on the next floor click. SelectItem no longer duplicates the check. B: WndBag hands its listener null on any close that is not a choice (windows/WndBag.java onBackPressed), via a VisibilityChanged handler guarded by a new _chosen flag set right before every choice's own Hide() call (a slot pick, a tab switch). C: GoldIndicator gets a ResetState() that GameScene.Build calls, so a level switch or Restart no longer shows the previous run's stale gold total. Confirmed against the Java: GoldIndicator is built fresh inside Toolbar.createChildren (ui/Toolbar.java), and Toolbar itself is rebuilt by GameScene.create() on every scene, including Restart. D: GameScene.Build recounts iron keys (Belongings.CountIronKeys) before RefreshQuickSlots, matching ui/StatusPane.java's createChildren, so the "Iron keys" readout no longer sticks to the previous depth's count after a level switch, console jump, or restart.

test: turn costs of item actions, and a lettered marker in MobAiTests F: MobAiTests' bare "DEFERRED(sp3): armour/Barkskin" comment violates the lettered-marker rule and was invisible to the marker audit (which scans only src/ and scripts/). Split it into "TODO: armour, TODO: Barkskin", matching where each actually lands. G: adds six turn-cost assertions the design spec's "## Tests" section calls for but nothing checked: a drop spends TIME_TO_DROP, a completed throw spends TIME_TO_THROW, a cancelled throw spends nothing, an adjacent chest spends TIME_TO_UNLOCK before OnOperateComplete, drinking the dew vial spends 1, and a pick-up spends 1. Each is a small sibling Fact next to the behaviour test it pins, using a shared SpyHero (moved from HeroTests into DungeonFixture so ItemActionTests, HeroItemTests and DewTests can all read Cooldown()). The drop and throw assertions were proven to bite: temporarily changing TIME_TO_DROP to 0.75f failed ExecuteDrop_SpendsTimeToDrop (expected 0.5, got 0.75), and TIME_TO_THROW to 1.5f failed Throw_Completed_SpendsTimeToThrow (expected 1, got 1.5), both constants were then reverted.

feat(core): buff icons and the armour-tier seam member BuffIndicator carries every constant from the Java. Buff.Icon() returns NONE unless a buff overrides it, and Amok, Terror, Cripple and Bleeding now do. ICharView gains UpdateArmor(int tier) for Armor's equip hooks: the null view ignores it, the test fake records each tier, and the Godot CharView stubs it until later.

feat(buffs): Poison, Paralysis, Slow and Roots The four afflictions port whole. Poison deals (int)(left / 3) + 1 a turn and records its death cause. Paralysis and Roots set and clear their Char flags, and Roots will not take hold of a flyer. Slow halves Char.Spend's time scale, so every action takes twice as long. Ring of Elements and the Frost check stay TODO.

feat(actors): affliction status texts, hero warnings and the snap-out Poison and Paralysis ship complete, as the 3b spec decides: - Char.Add shows "poisoned" with a poison splash, and "slowed", "paralysed" and "rooted". - Hero.Add warns on Paralysis, Poison and Roots, and the first two interrupt. - Char.Damage rolls Random.Int(dmg) against Random.Int(HP) to snap a paralysed character out, logging it when visible. - A poisoned Swarm splits into a clone poisoned for 2. The shared markers are split. Burning, Frost, Vertigo, Ooze and the rest stay TODO. MindVision, Levitation and Invisibility stay sp3c. The paralysed sprite state draws nothing, because the cubes have no animation to pause.
